content.title: Russian drones over Poland stir worries for Europe's airlines
content.description:
STORY: The incursion of Russian drones into Poland this week was yet another harsh reminder to airlines of the challenges presented by global conflicts.

Poland shot down the drones in its airspace with the support of military aircraft from NATO allies.

But aviation and insurance experts say it has led to safety concerns over the vulnerability of civil air transport in Europe.

At least four key airports in Poland were temporarily closed before resuming operations.

Growing conflict zones around the world have raised the burden on airline operations and profitability.

Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary warned Thursday the Russia-Ukraine war would be an ongoing issue for all European airlines for years to come.

Carriers face fewer route options with airspace closures in multiple regions, including Russia, Ukraine and the Middle East.

Detours then add to fuel costs and lengthen journey times.

The coordination agency Eurocontrol has said Ukraine's closed airspace has added to congestion in the region's skies.

Many international carriers have suspended flights to the area due to fears of missile and drone interference.

They are also keeping a close eye on conflict in the Middle East, including Israel's attempt on Tuesday to kill Hamas leaders in Qatar. 

Worries about further disruption for the travel industry are pressuring airline stocks.

Shares in British Airways owner IAG fell around 4% Wednesday following the latest incident, while easyJet, Lufthansa and Ryanair also fell.

One expert said airlines may now review their risk assessments in Poland.

While two senior aviation insurance sources said the market was watching events in Poland and Qatar closely.

content.title: Boeing steps up jet deliveries, surpassing 2024 total by August
content.summary: Boeing said on Tuesday that it delivered 57 jets in August, up from 48 in July. It was the highest number of deliveries in August since 2018, when the U.S. planemaker handed over 64 airliners. Deliveries last year were hampered in part by a seven-week strike by union workers in the Seattle area, though that stoppage did not begin until September.
